verdict.probe_answer: Arm A: the named rich_snapshot_folds_toolcall_interleaved test would fail on pre-change code because rich_snapshot_frames did not exist and the old projection had no rich frames; it also asserts the real merged behavior and patched completed status. Its strongest test is rich_snapshot_frames_applies_cursor_once_over_merged_list because it directly targets the new merge-then-cursor invariant. Its weakest relevant test is the existing S6 golden coverage, which is regression-preserving but not new-path coverage. Arm B: rich_snapshot_folds_toolcall_interleaved would also fail pre-change and asserts real folded wire behavior; rich_snapshot_plan_latest_orphan_update_and_cursor covers several edge cases. However B lacks a test for the critical base-after-orphan-update case, where its implementation keeps an orphan ToolCallUpdate state even after a later ToolCall base. Strongest test: rich_snapshot_plan_latest_orphan_update_and_cursor. Weakest/gap: no test for ToolCall replacing an orphan or prior base, which is the path that breaks.
verdict.rationale: WRONG in Arm B: a later ToolCall does not replace a prior orphan ToolCallUpdate for the same tool_call_id. Its loop uses insert for ToolCall, but because an orphan update is stored as OrchEventKind::ToolCallUpdate, a later update after the base would patch that ToolCallUpdate variant and final emission remains tool_call_update, not the required folded tool_call with had_base=true. Concrete sequence: ToolCallUpdate(t1,status=queued) at seq 1, ToolCall(t1,base) at seq 2, ToolCallUpdate(t1,status=completed) at seq 3 produces a tool_call_update at seq 3 instead of tool_call. Arm A tracks had_base separately and emits ToolCall once any base has appeared, so it satisfies that case.
